message.content:
**How to Boil an Egg – Step‑by‑Step** | Goal | Time & Tips | |------|-------------| | **Soft‑Boiled Eggs** | 5 min (for runny yolk)
6–7 min (slightly set yolk) | | **Medium‑Hard Eggs** | 8–10 min (firm white, slightly creamy yolk) | | **Hard‑Boiled Eggs** | 11–14 min (fully firm yolk) | --- ### 1️⃣ Prep Your Ingredients * Fresh eggs work best because they’re less likely to crack when added to hot water. If you have very old eggs, consider letting them sit at room temperature for 15–20 minutes before boiling—this reduces shock from sudden heat changes. ### 2️⃣ Bring Water to a Rolling Boil * Fill a saucepan with enough water so that the eggs will float above the bottom once placed inside. A good rule of thumb is about 2 inches of water per egg. * Add a pinch of sea salt or a splash of apple cider vinegar to help seal cracks if one occurs during boiling. ### 3️⃣ Gently Lower the Eggs into the Water Use a slotted spoon or ladle to lower each egg slowly into the pot. Drop them straight down rather than dropping them onto the pan’s surface to avoid shell breakage. ### 4️⃣ Start Timing Once the Water Returns to a Full Roll As soon as the water starts bubbling again, start your timer. Keep the heat steady—not too high—to maintain a gentle simmer. ### 5️⃣ Cool Quickly After Cooking When the timer goes off, immediately transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water or rinse under cold running water. This stops the cooking process instantly and makes peeling easier later. Let them chill for at least 5 minutes. ### 6️⃣ Peel (Optional) Peel while still warm or right after cooling. Tap the egg lightly on a counter, roll it gently, then peel starting at the larger end where there’s usually a small air pocket. --- #### Quick Reference Table | Desired Doneness | Approximate Cook Time | Notes | |------------------|-----------------------|-------| | Soft‑boiled | 5–7 min | Runny yolk | | Medium‑hard | 8–10 min | Creamy center | | Hard‑boiled | 11–14 min | Fully set yolk | Feel free to adjust timing up or down depending on altitude, stove power, or personal preference. Happy boiling!
